activity.notes: Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk was elected the first President of Czechoslovakia on 14 November 1918. He was subsequently elected under the constitutional order in 1920 and re-elected in 1927 and 1934, serving continuously until his abdication for health reasons on 14 December 1935. ATLAS records one continuous presidential Activity across those successive elections because there was no interruption in his tenure.

sources.title: Life and works in dates — Prague Castle
sources.citation_text: Prague Castle records Masaryk as the first President of the Czechoslovak Republic in 1918, his later presidential elections in 1920, 1927 and 1934, and his resignation in 1935.

sources.title: Osobnost v čele státu — Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic
sources.citation_text: The Czech Ministry of the Interior records Masaryk's fourth presidential election and states that he abdicated on 14 December 1935.

sources.title: Historical record of 14 November 1918 — Senate of the Parliament of the Czech Republic
sources.citation_text: The Czech Senate's historical record identifies 14 November 1918 as the day Tomáš Masaryk was proclaimed the first President of the Czechoslovak Republic.
